fields.meta_title: Sign in Form Builder for Visitors and Sites | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a sign in form for your lobby or job site. Emergent messages each host on arrival and saves every visit to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Sign in Form That Tracks Who Comes and Goes
fields.hero_description: A sign in form turns a front door into a record of every visit. Describe who signs in, and Emergent builds the form and the log behind it.
fields.features_heading: What a Clipboard Sheet Never Did
fields.features_subheading: A paper sheet keeps names in handwriting and shows each one to the next visitor. These features give every visit its own record.
fields.feature_1:
The questions a front desk needs

Asks for the visitor's name and company, then the host from a dropdown list. The form stamps the time in, and a returning visitor's details fill in from their email address.
fields.feature_2:
Sign-out on the same screen

Records the sign-out time when a visitor taps their name on the way out. Each visit row keeps both times and the length of the stay, and any visit left open gets flagged at closing.
fields.feature_3:
A message to the host on arrival

Sends the host a Slack direct message or an email naming the visitor and the company they are from. Reception no longer phones around the building to find out who is expecting whom.
fields.feature_4:
A live list of who is on site

Shows everyone signed in at this moment, grouped by work area. A shift lead can open the list on a phone, and each name drops off as that person signs out of the building.
fields.feature_5:
Hours added up per person

Totals each person's hours for the month from their sign-in and sign-out times. The totals sit in a database you own, and any tool with an API can pull them for a report.
fields.feature_6:
The whole app in your GitHub

Exports the full sign-in app to GitHub on paid plans. A developer can extend it in code, for example by connecting a badge printer, or you can keep changing it with a plain prompt.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Places a Sign in Form Works
fields.tab_content_1:
Sam Keller hears about his visitor in Slack

Visitors at Fieldstone Architects sign in on a tablet in the lobby. Lena Ortiz types her name and company, picks Sam Keller from the host list and taps Sign in. Sam gets a Slack direct message at 2:04 PM naming her and Northwind Freight, and he walks out to meet her.
fields.tab_content_2:
Anyone on site after 6:00 PM goes to the shift lead

Contractors at Bayline Cold Storage sign in at the dock door with their company and work area, and sign out on the same tablet. The app sends the shift lead the names of anyone still signed in at 6:00 PM. Tonight two electricians from Voltline Electric never signed out, and Marcus Hale sees their names next to Freezer B.
fields.tab_content_3:
Buyers without an agent make the follow-up list

Linden Realty holds an open house at 18 Alder Lane on a Sunday afternoon. Each group signs in at the door and says whether they already work with an agent. In all, 14 groups came through, and the five with no agent reach listing agent Dana Whitfield by email at 5:00 PM.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every sign-out adds hours to the monthly total

Cedar Hollow Animal Rescue counts volunteer hours for its grant reports. Volunteers sign in and out on the kennel tablet, and each closed visit adds to that person's monthly total. This month shows 312 hours across five volunteers, while one visit has sat open for 14 hours waiting on the coordinator.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Sign in Form
fields.howto_description: Start with where people sign in and what should happen after they do. The fields follow from that.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide who the form is for
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Pick the device at the door
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the people who sign in and the reason you keep the record. An office lobby needs a host field. A job site needs the work area, and a volunteer program needs hours. Each purpose adds a field or two to the same short form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name, time in, and time out are the core of any sign-in record. Add company, host, or reason for the visit only when someone acts on the answer. On a busy morning, every extra field makes the line at the door longer.
fields.howto_step_3_des: A tablet on a stand works for most reception desks. A site without a desk can post the link by the entrance for people to open on their own phones. Test it at the real door, in that light, with gloves on if your crews wear them.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tell Emergent who signs in, which fields you need and who should hear about each arrival. It builds the form and a table that holds every visit, sign-out times included. A later change, such as a new person on the host list, takes one more prompt.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide what an open visit means when the building closes. Pick an hour and a person who receives the names still signed in at that point. Without the rule, missed sign-outs pile up and the hours in your reports stop matching reality.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Keep a paper backup in a drawer
fields.howto_step_6_des: Print a blank sheet for the day the tablet's battery dies or the network drops. Whoever runs the desk types those entries into the form afterward. The visit log stays complete, and nobody has to merge two records at the end of the month.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the log once a week
fields.howto_step_7_des: Look through the week's visits for patterns, such as hosts who never respond or one door where sign-outs keep getting missed. Each pattern points to a field or a rule that needs changing, and that change is one prompt away.

plan.angle: The top 10 splits between login screens for Google Forms, Microsoft Forms and a fitness app, the form builders' home pages, and printable sign-in sheets from eForms, Adobe and GoFormz. A clipboard sheet records a name and a time and stops there: the host is not told, nobody signs out, and the hours sit in handwriting. This page treats a sign in form as a front-desk log with a job after each entry: a host message, a closing-time check on who is still on site, an open house follow-up list and monthly volunteer hours, all in one table you own.

chip_prompts: Build a sign in form for my office lobby tablet that asks each visitor for their name, company, and host, and saves every visit with the time in.
When a visitor signs in at my front desk, send their host a Slack direct message with the visitor's name and company, or an email if the host is not on Slack.
Let visitors sign out by tapping their name on the same tablet I use for sign-in. Record the time out and length of stay, and send me anyone still signed in at 6:00 PM.
I run volunteer shifts. Add up each person's hours from their sign-in and sign-out times, and show me a monthly total per volunteer for grant reports.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Sign in Form That Tracks Who Comes and Goes' and meta title 'Sign in Form Builder for Visitors and Sites' cover the whole visitor-log job, not one feature.

intent.evidence: Top 10 mixes builders and printable sheets; page answers the PAA 'How do I sign in an online form?' and covers template, PDF, Word and free variants in the FAQ alongside four working builds.

specificity.evidence: 'Sam gets a Slack direct message at 2:04 PM naming her and Northwind Freight'; 'Test it at the real door, in that light, with gloves on if your crews wear them.'

openers.evidence: Feature bodies open on verbs ('Asks for', 'Records', 'Sends', 'Shows', 'Totals', 'Exports'); tabs open on full sentences ('Visitors at Fieldstone Architects sign in on a tablet in the lobby.').

craft.evidence: Short declaratives with one idea each; no blocking craft defect; repeated ideas recorded as notes.

voice.evidence: Plain operator voice: 'Print a blank sheet for the day the tablet's battery dies or the network drops.'

truth.evidence: Adobe Acrobat and Microsoft Create facts match domain_sources; free tier and no-cap claims map to free-start and no-caps; tab 4 hours 64+58+71+49+70=312 match the image.

distinct.evidence: Visitor, contractor, open house and volunteer stories are specific to sign-in logs; sibling sign-out-form takes school dismissal and hall passes.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic items, PAA 'How do I sign in an online form?' answered first sentence; hub link in item 2; sign up form, liability waiver form and emergency contact form links.

images.evidence: Contact sheet: 2:04 PM DM to Sam Keller, 2 still signed in at Freezer B, 14 groups with 5 no-agent emailed 5:00 PM, 312 hours with Jordan Lee open 14 hours, all as the tab copy says.
